# SUCC–FUCC affine critical-state theorem

**Date:** 2026-10-05  
**Status:** exact operator-algebraic control and prime-event realization. RH remains open.

## 1. The canonical algebra generated by SUCC and FUCC already exists

Let

\[
P=\mathbb N\rtimes\mathbb N^\times
\]

with product

\[
(m,a)(n,b)=(m+an,ab).
\]

Its Toeplitz \(C^*\)-algebra is generated by an additive isometry \(S\) and multiplicative isometries \(V_a\).

The exact affine relation is

\[
\boxed{V_aS=S^aV_a.}
\]

The multiplicative operators commute,

\[
V_aV_b=V_bV_a,
\]

but the additive and multiplicative generators do not.

The Nica covariance formula is

\[
W_{(m,a)}^*W_{(n,b)}
=
0
\]

unless

\[
m\equiv n\pmod{\gcd(a,b)},
\]

and when the congruence is satisfied the product is an explicit affine partial isometry determined by the Euclidean algorithm.

Thus the cross terms of SUCC and FUCC are controlled exactly by gcd/congruence arithmetic.

Primary source: Laca–Raeburn, arXiv:0907.3760, Theorem 4.1 and Lemmas 4.3–4.4.

## 2. The affine KMS temperature is shifted by one additive dimension

For the Toeplitz affine system, there is a unique KMS_beta state for

\[
1\le\beta\le2.
\]

Laca–Neshveyev show that its multiplicative component is the symmetric Bost–Connes equilibrium state at inverse temperature

\[
\beta_{\mathrm{BC}}=\beta_{\mathrm{aff}}-1.
\]

Therefore the Bost–Connes critical half-density value

\[
\beta_{\mathrm{BC}}=\frac12
\]

corresponds exactly to

\[
\boxed{
\beta_{\mathrm{aff}}=\frac32.
}
\]

This is the canonical equilibrium point of the coupled SUCC–FUCC system relevant to the critical line.

Primary source: Laca–Neshveyev, arXiv:1010.0599, Proposition 2.1 / Theorem 2.5 and the beta-minus-one identification.

## 3. Exact KMS monomial formula

For \(1\le\beta\le2\), the unique KMS state \(\phi_\beta\) satisfies

\[
\boxed{
\phi_\beta(
S^mV_aV_b^*S^{*n}
)
=
\begin{cases}
a^{-\beta},&a=b,\ m=n,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
}
\]

This is equation (9.1) in Laca–Raeburn.

Thus distinct affine branches are orthogonal in the KMS GNS metric.

## 4. SUCC residue degeneracy produces the RH half-density

For \(a\ge1\), define the mutually orthogonal residue-branch range projections

\[
e_{r,a}
=
S^rV_aV_a^*S^{*r},
\qquad
0\le r<a.
\]

Their sum

\[
E_a=\sum_{r=0}^{a-1}e_{r,a}
\]

is the diagonal projection that forgets the residue and remembers only the multiplicative depth condition \(a\mid N\) in the Nica-spectrum coordinate.

Each branch has KMS weight

\[
\phi_\beta(e_{r,a})=a^{-\beta}.
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{
\phi_\beta(E_a)
=
a^{1-\beta}.
}
\]

At the SUCC–FUCC critical value \(\beta=3/2\),

\[
\boxed{
\phi_{3/2}(E_a)
=
a^{-1/2}.
}
\]

Therefore the half-density is exactly

\[
\boxed{
\underbrace{a}_{\text{SUCC residue degeneracy}}
\times
\underbrace{a^{-3/2}}_{\text{FUCC affine KMS weight}}
=
a^{-1/2}.
}
\]

This explains the beta shift geometrically.

## 5. Prime-power event weights are affine KMS expectations

For a prime power \(q=p^k\),

\[
\frac{\Lambda(q)}{\sqrt q}
=
(\log p)\phi_{3/2}(E_q).
\]

Therefore the Suzuki finite-prime ramp is exactly the expectation of the positive diagonal affine observable

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal P_t
=
\sum_{q=p^k}
\Lambda(q)(t-\log q)_+\,E_q,
}
\]

namely

\[
\boxed{
P(t)
=
\phi_{3/2}(\mathcal P_t).
}
\]

The sum is finite for every fixed \(t\), and \(\mathcal P_t\ge0\).

This is an exact SUCC+FUCC realization of the entire prime ramp.

## 6. Fourier-symmetrized FUCC modes

Let

\[
\omega_q=e^{2\pi i/q}
\]

and define the affine Fourier branch operator

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal W_q
=
\sum_{r=0}^{q-1}
\omega_q^r S^rV_q.
}
\]

Using

\[
V_q^*S^jV_q=0,\qquad 1\le |j|<q,
\]

one gets

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal W_q^*\mathcal W_q=qI.
}
\]

Let \((\pi_\beta,\mathcal H_\beta,\Omega_\beta)\) be the GNS representation of \(\phi_\beta\), and set

\[
\xi_q=\pi_\beta(\mathcal W_q)^*\Omega_\beta.
\]

Then the monomial KMS formula gives

\[
\boxed{
\langle\xi_q,\xi_r\rangle
=
\delta_{qr}\,q^{1-\beta}.
}
\]

At \(\beta=3/2\),

\[
\boxed{
\|\xi_q\|^2=q^{-1/2}.
}
\]

Thus the q residue branches have coherently compressed into one orthogonal FUCC mode whose norm is precisely the critical half-density.

## 7. Modular frequency is logarithmic FUCC energy

The affine dynamics fixes \(S\) and satisfies

\[
\sigma_t(V_q)=q^{it}V_q.
\]

Hence

\[
\sigma_t(\mathcal W_q)=q^{it}\mathcal W_q.
\]

In the KMS GNS representation, the vector \(\xi_q=\mathcal W_q^*\Omega\) is a modular eigenvector with frequency \(-\log q\).

Choose the positive frequency generator \(L\) so that

\[
\boxed{
L\xi_q=(\log q)\xi_q.
}
\]

Therefore the critical prime-power event coordinate \(\log q\) is literally the modular FUCC energy of the affine mode.

## 8. The exact prime event measure is a modular spectral measure

Restrict to prime powers and define the locally finite generalized vector

\[
\Xi_{\mathrm{pp}}
=
\sum_{q=p^k}
\sqrt{\Lambda(q)}\,\xi_q.
\]

It is not globally Hilbert because its total norm diverges, but every bounded spectral cutoff is a finite vector.

Its local spectral measure for \(L\) is exactly

\[
\boxed{
d\mu_{\Xi}(\lambda)
=
\sum_{q=p^k}
\frac{\Lambda(q)}{\sqrt q}
\delta_{\log q}(d\lambda).
}
\]

Thus Suzuki's distributional prime curvature is the modular spectral measure of the SUCC–FUCC prime-power field.

For every \(t\),

\[
\boxed{
P(t)
=
\left\|
(t-L)_+^{1/2}
\Xi_{\mathrm{pp}}
\right\|^2,
}
\]

understood through the finite spectral cutoff implicit in \((t-L)_+\).

This is a manifestly positive exact formula.

## 9. Von Mangoldt arises from modular energy divided by tower depth

On the one-prime sector \(q=p^k\), define the tower-depth operator

\[
K\xi_{p^k}=k\,\xi_{p^k}.
\]

Then

\[
LK^{-1}\xi_{p^k}
=
(\log p)\xi_{p^k}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\frac{\Lambda(p^k)}{\sqrt{p^k}}
=
\left\langle
\xi_{p^k},
LK^{-1}\xi_{p^k}
\right\rangle.
}
\]

No logarithmic derivative is needed to explain the cancellation of k:

- modular energy gives \(k\log p\);
- primitive/tower normalization divides by depth \(k\);
- the KMS GNS norm supplies \(p^{-k/2}\).

This is an operator-theoretic realization of the exact von Mangoldt weight.

## 10. The additive/multiplicative cross term is intrinsic

For the concrete positive-number representation,

\[
S|n\rangle=|n+1\rangle,
\qquad
V_a|n\rangle=|an\rangle,
\]

and

\[
V_aS=S^aV_a.
\]

If

\[
H|n\rangle=(\log n)|n\rangle,
\]

then

\[
\boxed{
S^*[H,S]
=
\log(1+N^{-1}),
}
\]

the logarithmic proper-time length of one successor edge, while

\[
\boxed{
[H,V_a]
=
(\log a)V_a.
}
\]

Thus the same Hamiltonian \(H=\log N\) simultaneously measures:

- local SUCC edge lengths;
- exact FUCC scale displacement.

It is the canonical metric bridge between the two operations.

## 11. Gamma as renormalized SUCC–FUCC curvature holonomy

Compare the two affine paths

\[
n\overset{S}{\longrightarrow}n+1
\overset{\times m}{\longrightarrow}m(n+1)
\]

and

\[
n\overset{\times m}{\longrightarrow}mn
\overset{S}{\longrightarrow}mn+1.
\]

Their logarithmic endpoint mismatch is

\[
\kappa_m(n)
=
\log\frac{m(n+1)}{mn+1}
=
\log\left(1+\frac1n\right)
-
\log\left(1+\frac1{mn}\right)
>0.
\]

The accumulated curvature is

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{N}\kappa_m(n)
=
\log
\frac{
\Gamma(N+2)\Gamma(1+1/m)
}{
\Gamma(N+1+1/m)
}.
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{
\lim_{N\to\infty}
\left[
\sum_{n=1}^{N}\kappa_m(n)
-
\left(1-\frac1m\right)\log N
\right]
=
\log\Gamma\left(1+\frac1m\right).
}
\]

Set

\[
z=\frac1m.
\]

Then

\[
\log\Gamma(z)
=
\left[
\text{renormalized SUCC–FUCC holonomy at }m=1/z
\right]
-\log z.
\]

In particular, with \(z=s/2\),

\[
\boxed{
\log L_\infty(s)
=
-\frac{s}{2}\log\pi
+
\log\Gamma(s/2)
}
\]

is the renormalized Archimedean affine holonomy plus elementary normalization.

Thus the Gamma factor is not foreign to the SUCC–FUCC geometry: it is the regularized cumulative noncommutativity of additive and multiplicative motion at the real place.

## 12. Consecutive integers are maximally transverse in FUCC coordinates

Unique factorization gives occupation vectors

\[
v(n)=(v_p(n))_p.
\]

Since

\[
\gcd(n,n+1)=1,
\]

the positive supports of \(v(n)\) and \(v(n+1)\) are disjoint.

Hence every SUCC step destroys all occupied multiplicative modes of the old integer and creates a disjoint collection for the next integer.

The additive path is therefore maximally nonlocal in the multiplicative coordinate basis.

This is a structural reason that a bare n-line cannot carry the RH metric.

## 13. Positive primitive projection by chaos rather than logarithm

At the critical multiplicative product state, the local valuation depths are independent geometric variables.

Therefore

\[
L^2(\mu_{1/2})
=
\bigotimes_p
\left(
\mathbb C1\oplus H_p^0
\right)
\]

has the orthogonal Hoeffding/Fock decomposition

\[
L^2
=
\bigoplus_{S\subset_{\mathrm{fin}}\mathcal P}
\bigotimes_{p\in S}H_p^0.
\]

The one-prime sector

\[
\bigoplus_p H_p^0
\]

is a canonical positive-Hilbert "primitive/connected" sector, while higher tensor chaoses contain cross-prime composite fluctuations.

This supplies a positivity-preserving primitive projection that is different from the ordinary Dirichlet logarithm refuted in Round 003.

It does not yet prove that the projected Suzuki screw kernel is positive.

## 14. The exact remaining proof obligation

The finite-prime side is now fully represented inside the coupled SUCC–FUCC affine KMS geometry.

The missing theorem is an Archimedean/global comparison:

> Construct a canonical vector/operator in the affine/adelic GNS space whose projection onto the prime-power modular modes has squared norm \(P(t)\), while its total squared norm is exactly \(A_\infty(t)\), or whose stationary-increment Gram pullback is \(K_\Psi\) up to a uniformly bounded Brownian lift.

Pointwise version:

\[
\boxed{
\|\operatorname{Proj}_{\rm pp}\eta_t\|^2=P(t),
\qquad
\|\eta_t\|^2=A_\infty(t).
}
\]

Then Bessel/Pythagoras would give

\[
\Psi(t)=A_\infty(t)-P(t)\ge0
\]

and hence RH.

No such \(\eta_t\) has been constructed here. This is the precise noncircular seam.
